name: SVC_CSS_IDP_MIGR_HISTORY
description: This table is used to store the history of migrations of users between two identity providers. EVENT_ID is primary / unique key in this table.

columns.name: EVENT_ID
columns.description: Serial number and primary key for this table.

columns.name: JOB_ID
columns.description: An identifier that is generated every time a new job is started.

columns.name: CONTACT_PARTY_ID
columns.description: Party ID of the contact to be migrated.

columns.name: EVENT_TYPE_CD
columns.description: This column will identify the event type, which will be in the form of a LOV.

columns.name: MIGRATION_TYPE_CD
columns.description: This column will store the migration type for a particular event, which will be in the form of a LOV.

columns.name: LOGIN_ID
columns.description: Login ID of the contact to be migrated.

columns.name: FA_GUID
columns.description: GUID of the contact that exists in FA.

columns.name: IDCS_GUID
columns.description: GUID of the contact that exists in IDCS.

columns.name: EVENT_STATUS_CD
columns.description: This column will store the status code of an event, which will be in the form of a LOV.

columns.name: EVENT_NOTE
columns.description: This column will store useful information about the status of the event. If there are any exceptions that occur during the course of an event, then this column will store that information.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.
